# Bun is pinned (not "latest") for reproducibility. Since worldgen v11 the pin
# is no longer load-bearing for the worldgen hash tests — seed-determined noise
# is bit-portable across JS engines (lib/world/noise.ts, proven by
# e2e/determinism.e2e.ts) — so a Bun bump should NOT shift those digests; if it
# ever does, that's a portability bug, not a re-baseline. See docs/testing.md.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run lint
      - run: bun run typecheck
      - run: bun run format:check
      - run: bun test
      - run: bun run build
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"

  e2e:
    # Browser e2e takes several times longer than verify, so it gates merges
    # to main (the push event), not every PR iteration — PRs still run the
    # full verify job, and renderer/input/shell work runs e2e locally per
    # AGENTS.md before landing.
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.12"
      - run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - run: bun run test:e2e
        env:
          NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

  # ── Deploy only after the whole gate is green (verify AND e2e), and only on a
  # push to main. A red CI never ships. Platform on-push auto-deploys are OFF
  # (Vercel via vercel.json git.deploymentEnabled; Fly in its dashboard), so
  # these jobs are the sole deploy trigger. Each serializes across pushes on its
  # own concurrency group so overlapping merges release in order, not on top of
  # each other. See docs/deploy.md.
  deploy-web:
    needs: [verify, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5 # a hung deploy must not squat the (never-cancelled) slot
    permissions: {} # only curls an external hook — no repo-scoped token needed
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-web-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      # Fire the Vercel Deploy Hook. Hook-triggered builds stay Git-connected, so
      # VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA (the menu version badge) is still populated. -f
      # fails the job on a non-2xx; --max-time caps a hung request.
      - run: curl -fsS --max-time 30 -X POST "${{ secrets.VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL }}"

  deploy-server:
    needs: [verify, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20 # remote Fly build + rollout; bounds a hung deploy
    permissions:
      contents: read # checkout only; the deploy authenticates with FLY_API_TOKEN
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-server-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false # flyctl uses FLY_API_TOKEN, not the git credential
      # Pinned to an immutable SHA (not @master): this job holds FLY_API_TOKEN,
      # so a mutable ref would be a supply-chain risk.
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@ed8efb33836e8b2096c7fd3ba1c8afe303ebbff1 # v1.6
      # The exact config the manual deploy uses — NEVER a bare `flyctl deploy`:
      # the repo root has no Dockerfile, so flyctl's scanner would ship the
      # Next.js web image to the game-server app and crash-loop it (deploy.md).
      # --remote-only builds on Fly's builders (no Docker daemon in the runner).
      - run: flyctl deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --remote-only
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}

content.text:
Because the fix can only be *verified* in CI, and CI's e2e doesn't run on PRs by default.

The chain of reasoning:

1. **These flakes are CI-only.** Every one of them passes on my machine (macOS, hardware GL) and fails on GitHub's runner (ubuntu, software GL) — I proved that when the touch/multiplayer fixes passed locally but the merge run still went red. So "it passes locally" tells me nothing; the only real test is a run on the actual CI runner.

2. **e2e is wired to run *only* on push-to-main** (`ci.yml`: `if: github.event_name == 'push'`). On a normal PR it's *skipped* — deliberately, so PRs stay fast. That means without a change, I'd get zero e2e signal on this fix branch.

3. **The alternatives are worse:**
   - Push each attempt straight to `main` and watch e2e there → clutters main history, and every red run is the *deploy gate* blocking (and each green one would deploy). Iterating experimental flake-fixes directly on main/prod is messy.
   - Trust local and merge blind → that's exactly what already failed.

   Temporarily letting e2e run on *this PR* lets me iterate against the real runner **without touching main** — and the **deploy jobs stay `main`-only**, so nothing deploys off the PR.

4. **It's temporary and self-flagged.** The commit and PR both say the `|| pull_request` trigger must be reverted to push-only before merge, so the normal policy (e2e gates merges, not every PR) is restored. If I forget, the merge would just keep running e2e on future PRs — no correctness or deploy risk, only extra CI minutes.

So: it's a scaffolding to get real-CI feedback on a branch. If you'd rather not spend CI minutes this way — I could instead iterate directly on main (accepting the messy history), or fall back to de-scoping the touch e2e from the gate entirely. But given you chose "fix the flakes," running them where they actually fail is the only way to know if a fix works. Want me to keep going, or change tack?

The CI run finished — and this is decisive. **With all my fixes + retries bumped to 3, the touch tests still fail**, and worse, the drag test that *passed* last run now flaked. Meanwhile **everything non-touch is fine**:

| Test | Result this run |
|---|---|
| `touch.ts:34` joystick | ❌ hard fail (discrete-moves fix didn't hold) |
| `touch.ts:83` mineHeld | ❌ hard fail (was flaky — got *worse*; 10s poll didn't help) |
| `touch.ts:149` options-toggle | ❌ hard fail (force-click → now a 60s timeout) |
| `touch.ts:58` drag | ⚠️ flaky (*passed* last run — regressed) |
| `determinism.ts:13` | ⚠️ flaky (retry-passed) |
| **everything else** (multiplayer, smoke, pwa, menu, …) | ✅ **passed** |

This is the exact scenario I flagged: **the touch e2e suite is intractably flaky in headless software-GL.** Four different touch tests flake/fail *inconsistently* across runs — my targeted fixes (discrete moves, force-click, longer polls) didn't stabilize them because the root cause is synthetic-pointer-in-headless timing, not something a test tweak fixes. Continuing would burn many more 26-min runs with low confidence.

The important thing: **if I de-scope the touch e2e from CI, the gate goes green** — the only non-touch flake is determinism, which retries cover.

And the coverage loss is small: the touch *gesture logic* is already unit-tested deterministically in `touchInputController.test.ts`, and touch has a **real-device manual pass** per AGENTS.md. The e2e was only exercising the DOM journey — the least reliable thing to drive headlessly.

So we're at the decision point I pre-flagged:

options.description: Skip touch.e2e.ts when process.env.CI is set (still runs locally + covered by touchInputController.test.ts unit tests + the real-device manual pass per AGENTS.md). e2e gate then goes green on the deterministic suites, unblocking the deploy. Keep my other fixes (chest timeout, retries=3).

options.label: Keep grinding on the touch fixes
